best_for: Engineers, analysts and students who draw flowcharts, network maps or UML and want the files on their own disk, with no account and no bill.
description:
draw.io is a diagram editor from JGraph, which runs it through draw.io Ltd and draw.io AG. The company says it is independent and not funded by venture capital, and it has made the editor since 2005. This desktop app wraps the same core editor in its own window.

Choose between the Sketch, Classic and Simple interface styles. A file you make here also opens in the web editor and in draw.io's add-ons for Google Drive, Confluence, Jira and VS Code, and anyone can open and edit it without a license. You can embed an interactive diagram in a wiki or web page, too. On Windows, a portable zip build runs without installing anything.

points.title: Free, with no paid tier to hit
points.text: draw.io costs nothing and needs no sign-up or card to start. There is no premium plan that gates shapes or exports. The desktop app is GPL-3.0 and the core editor is Apache 2.0.

points.title: Your diagrams stay offline
points.text: The desktop app does not load remote code and sends no diagram data or usage analytics. The only call home is the update check. A diagram that links to outside images or fonts will still fetch those when you open it.

points.title: Opens old files, exports common ones
points.text: Diagrams made as far back as 2005 still open. You can export to PNG, SVG or PDF, or keep the diagram editable inside the exported image.

points.title: Pick the Windows installer by need
points.text: The .exe installer sets up the app for all users and needs administrator rights. The MSI installs for the current user only. The Windows listing keeps 124 versions, in x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Updates differ by build
points.text: The Windows .exe, macOS and AppImage builds update themselves in the background. The MSI only tells you a new release exists. Flatpak updates come through Flathub. You can turn update checks off from the Extras menu or with `--disable-update`.

points.title: Help is best effort
points.text: Support runs through the GitHub issue tracker only, with no private tickets, and the project does not accept outside code contributions. Buying draw.io for Confluence or Jira does not add support for the desktop app.

points.title: Mac and Linux listings hold one version
points.text: macOS builds need macOS 13 or later, for Intel and Apple silicon. The Linux Flatpak is published under JGraph's name but Flathub does not mark it as verified. Both list only the current release, so downgrades there need the GitHub releases page.
